question: Does current Ninja generation retain a working-directory command when every declared custom command evaluates empty, preventing the existing phony fallback and leaving Windows with a bare cd /D command?

sources.name: CMake issue 24802
sources.claim: The reported failure concerns Ninja build statements generated from empty custom commands on Windows.

sources.name: Kitware/CMake GitHub mirror
sources.claim: Current master source retains the working-directory line before filtering evaluated-empty commands and already has a phony fallback when the final command-line vector is empty.

environment.runtime: CMake 3.31.6; Ninja 1.12.1 for the executable Linux control; CMake master 457b8a2acb76d0331889955b1ab74b0d21357ddf for source mapping
environment.platform: linux-x86_64 control plus deterministic _WIN32 source-path analysis

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: The evaluated-empty fixture generates CUSTOM_COMMAND with only COMMAND = cd <build-dir>; current master emits cd /D under _WIN32 and does not wrap a single such line in cmd.exe.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: Supports the reported Windows command-emission defect and identifies the stray working-directory line as the blocker preventing the existing phony fallback.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: After removing that lone working-directory line when no real command survives, cmdLines becomes empty.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The existing WriteCustomCommandBuildStatement phony branch becomes the natural no-command path; no new Ninja rule semantics are required.

stop_condition: Stop after the current generated rule, current master source path, existing phony fallback, and smallest source/test candidate are identified. Execute the candidate on the user's CMake fork before any upstream submission.
network_policy: disabled for the reproducer; public source inspection used the connected GitHub mirror
